question.text: A GOI 10-year bond futures is priced at Rs. 104.50 and the underlying spot bond price is Rs. 104.20. If the net carry (financing cost after income) is 0.50%, what is the theoretical futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Bond futures pricing uses cash price + financing cost - income on cash position. When the 0.50% is stated as net carry (financing cost net of income), the theoretical price = 104.20 * (1 + 0.005) = 104.721, which rounds to Rs. 104.72. The Trap: Rs. 104.50 is the market price, not the theoretical price. Rs. 104.70 just adds 0.50 to spot, and Rs. 105.20 adds 1.00; cost of carry must be applied as a percentage of spot. Note: The 0.50% here is treated as net carry only because the stem says so. If the bond's accrued or coupon income is given separately, you would need to deduct it: theoretical = cash price + financing cost - income on cash position.
